Peking, June 19.

label: text
text: Following a meeting of the diplomatic representatives of the interested Powers this morning, a communique was issued stating: The delegation of interested diplomatic representatives went to Shanghai solely on a mission of investigation. Later it had its powers enlarged and was brought into negotiation's with the Chinese delegates. The last named having presented demands which exceeded the powers of the delegation, the latter took note of the fact and is returning to make a report. The interested diplomatic representatives have already made known to the Wachiaopu their desire to begin negotiations without delay. In their opinion, immediate settlement of the Shanghai incidents themselves on a basis of justice and equity must be the object of a first agreement. Likewise if the Chinese Government expresses a desire the interested diplomatic representatives are disposed to request their respective Governments for authorisation to discuss in the friendliest spirit the propositions presented to their delegation in Shanghai concerning both the organisation of the International Settlement and the administration of justice therein.

text: Last night the s.s. Fatshan, owned by the China Navigation Co. and operated in conjunction with the Steamboat Co., did not sail for Canton although the Chinese crew were ready to stand by. This is explained by the fact that the rumoured general strike in Canton and other parts of China was due to commence this morning. The Steamboat Co.'s Kinshan did not sail for Canton this morning and it is not likely that another vessel will go up to night. label: paragraph_title
text: Queen's College.

label: text
text:
With the University of Hong Kong on vacation Queen's College, as the principal Government educational institution, has been made the mark of irresponsible elements since the Shanghai disturbances began and letters abusive and threatening have been received by the senior students. Intimidation by means of threats unless the students abstained from attending College were made in some cases in the main streets by persons of workmanlike appearance.
There has been no excitement of any kind but 250 of the senior boys have absented themselves as from Thursday morning. The junior school remained at the time practically unaffected but there are more absences reported this morning. Close on 300 students all told are; however, carrying on their studies as usual.
It is reported that the dissatisfaction of Queen's College was to be the commencement of a general student strike in the Colony but all other school's appear to be carrying on as usual.
